notes.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy says a supertanker with over 2 million barrels and a gas carrier struck mines in the strait and caught fire.
Iran's IRIB agency carries an IRGC claim that three more tankers hit mines east of Hormuz; no names, flags or casualties given, and UKMTO and CENTCOM have not commented.
UKMTO separately reported a tanker hit by an unknown projectile 13km north of Khasab, Oman, with an engine-room fire and no casualties; a link to the mine claims is unclear.
CENTCOM said in November that main lanes are clear of mines and more than 3,000 ships passed in six months with US naval support; it rejected an earlier Iranian mine claim.
A US defense official says fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island in self-defence after Iranian attacks on US assets.
Iran fired on a US air base in Kuwait and at Bahrain; both Gulf states say they intercepted the attacks and neither reported damage or casualties.
notes.event: Iranian attack on Kuwait and Bahrain

notes.fact: AP reports Iran widened attacks after about two months without them; Bahrain, home to the US 5th Fleet, has been hit repeatedly in recent days.
notes.event: Iranian attack on Kuwait and Bahrain

notes.fact: Reuters says the nearly nine-month Iran war has raised gasoline prices in the US and worldwide, and voter anger helped Republicans lose in Congress two weeks ago.
notes.event: US fuel prices and the Iran war

notes.fact: A Globe and Mail headline says Trump is unlikely to resume strikes on Iran if talks progress; article text was not available.
Iran International reports Foreign Minister Araghchi proposed Hormuz de-escalation steps within two days, while hardliners such as Rezaei argue Iran has won and oppose compromise.
NewsNation reports DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullins says Iran has been attempting cyberattacks on the US since February.
Reuters says Ukraine struck the Crimea bridge a third time in a week, suspending trains, according to Russian authorities, hours before Putin met Xi and Trump.
The Kyiv Independent says Zelensky described the Nov 17 Flamingo missile strike as the last phase of a seven-phase operation lasting several weeks.
Kyiv outlet NV reports at least 15 blasts in Kerch overnight; Russian-installed head Aksyonov confirmed the attack and a rail halt, and a Telegram channel reports Sevastopol fuel queues.
Reuters notes Russia's military already relies more on the land corridor through occupied southern Ukraine than on the bridge, which limits the logistics effect.
SFG Media says fallen structure could hinder large vessels between the Black Sea and Azov; a Ukrainian analyst told Kyiv Independent debris clearing is needed to restore shipping access.
CNN reports Trump, Xi and Putin held about 90 minutes of trilateral talks in Shenzhen at APEC, per China's CCTV; Trump said Iran, Ukraine and trade were on the agenda.
RT, Russian state-funded media, quotes Trump as optimistic about Ukraine and Putin saying Ukraine took up much of his bilateral with Trump.
Kyiv Post says Kyiv and European leaders were excluded, and Zelensky called Trump's one-on-one with Putin a mistake.
Al Jazeera analysts say Moscow's minimum demands (all of Donbas, no Ukrainian NATO bid) are unchanged and the meeting is unlikely to alter the war's course.
Fox News reports Trump saying he and Xi agree Iran must not have a nuclear weapon and both want the Strait of Hormuz open.
The Israeli army told AFP it launched a precise operation west of the Yellow Line to remove a threat; Gaza civil defence reports three people killed in drone strikes.
notes.event: Israeli ground operation beyond Yellow Line

notes.fact: Times of Israel says the army targeted a tunnel in blocks near Bureij and Nuseirat, with evacuation orders unusual since the October 2025 ceasefire.
notes.event: Israeli ground operation beyond Yellow Line

notes.fact: Al Jazeera calls it the first major publicly announced ground offensive since the Oct 10, 2025 ceasefire and says the US-backed Board of Peace warned the deal risks collapse.
notes.event: Israeli ground operation beyond Yellow Line

notes.fact: The Israeli military told AFP the operation is complete and COGAT says Salah al-Din road has reopened; Gaza's ministry counts over 1,600 killed since the ceasefire.

notes.fact: Defense Minister Katz said further escalation could see Israel seize more territory and make it permanent security zones, per Common Dreams, a US progressive outlet.

notes.fact: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted missiles fired toward Riyadh and four toward the south; Houthis claim they targeted Riyadh's airport and financial centre.
AFP witnesses say Riyadh's 80-storey Public Investment Fund tower was damaged; the coalition says debris fell, and a past airport attack killed 14, per AFP.
Saudi authorities say at least 26 people have been killed in suspected Houthi attacks in the kingdom since September 23.
Al Jazeera says Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, a key export route given Hormuz limits, was damaged and has been attacked several times.
Al Jazeera notes the deal text and timelines were not released and the Pentagon had not announced the trip in advance.
AFRICOM says it struck al-Shabaab near Leego on Nov 12 and at three sites between Nov 13 and 15, near Leego, Yora Lafagari and Jamaame.
Antiwar.com says AFRICOM has announced at least 92 Somalia strikes in 2026 and a reporter says al-Shabaab killed at least eight Danab soldiers on Nov 12; single-source.
Somalia's intelligence agency says two al-Shabaab members, including a finance chief, were killed in Hiraan with help from international partners; Turkish state agency Anadolu relays it.
IAEA chief Grossi says an extension to the Yongbyon enrichment plant, begun mid-September, was externally complete by late October, calling it a serious concern.
SCMP and Al Jazeera note IAEA inspectors have been absent since 2009; Pyongyang's foreign minister rejected a G7 call for disarmament and Kim Yo-jong calls its nuclear status absolute.
Secretary of State Rubio says there is zero evidence the recent tech outages are linked or caused by hackers or foreign governments; the DNI sees no sign of coordination.
Deseret News lists a week of outages at Microsoft, the FAA, Chase, United and Apple; the White House says no sign of state-sponsored activity, and online claims of a Chinese attack lack evidence.
CSIS says Iran-linked hackers hit US water systems in at least 12 states in August; CyberAv3ngers claimed it, the US has not formally attributed it, and disruption was limited.
Targeted devices included Schneider Electric and Siemens controllers also used in US utilities; CISA and FBI advise taking them off the internet and enabling multifactor authentication.
Konbriefing's tracker lists Ridgecrest Regional Hospital, California, with phone and computer systems disrupted and the extent of the suspected attack unclear.
